newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: INSTANT VIEW - Mandela's speech to parliament.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Mandela's speech to parliament.

text.p: The following are a selection of reactions to President Nelson Mandela's speech to parliament on Friday. Mandela started his address at 0900 GMT and was still speaking at 1010 GMT:

"It reaffirms that the government will continue its steady path of liberalising the economy and that there are unlikely to be any major surprises. That's particularly important for investors because a predictable liberalising environment is clearly preferable to sudden lurches in policy."
"The speech is a good reaffirmation of a sound policy direction but there is nothing substantially new in it."
"It's broadly positive. There's nothing specific, but we didn't expect anything specific...The privatisation news seems to be quite good."

"It's good he affirmed the government's commitment to privatisation, and the almost immediate privatisation of Telkom, Aventura and Sunair...that's certainly a step in the right direction. The phased relaxation of exchange controls was expected. It's a bit unfortunate that we don't have any further information on how that will be done or a plan of action, but hopefully that will be forthcoming."
DAVE MOHR, OLD MUTUAL, CAPE TOWN

"There's nothing startling in there but it reaffirms the sound direction of policy overall...people who expected major specifics on economic policy were expecting too much from this kind of forum. What is encouraging is that he is talking about the accelerated implementation of GEAR (Growth, Employment and Restribution strategy). Of course, expectations have now been raised and this must be followed by actions in the budget."
